issues.tldr: AI-driven offensive tooling dominated the cycle: Switzerland and Italy confirmed autonomous AI agents breached critical-infrastructure operators, and Accenture flagged suspected AI-assisted exploitation of Mitel's MiCollab zero-days. CISA added 15 actively exploited CVEs to its KEV catalog in 48 hours, while 1Password, FinCEN, and FIFA all disclosed breaches.

A heavy exploitation day: CISA added 12 actively-exploited CVEs to its KEV catalog, including a critical Drupal RCE ("Fail2Install") with a Nov 27 federal patch deadline and an N-able Mail Assure bug that caused a week-long email outage. Separately, 1Password, FinCEN, and FIFA all disclosed breaches, and a suspected AI-automated campaign ("GT13") hit 24 Check Point management servers across 22 organizations.

A heavy day for actively exploited bugs — CISA added five flaws to its KEV catalog (N-able Mail Assure, Drupal, Optimizely, MONAI Label, Idunno AntiCsrf) and VMware patched a new critical vCenter bug alongside an already-exploited China-nexus vCenter zero-day. Breaches piled up at South Korea's KEPCO (1.5M records), Colorado's myColorado ID app (~150K), LaLiga, the European Commission, and an unclassified CIA system, while two separate reports pointed to AI agents increasingly running attacks on their own.

Lighter news cycle today — only 8 items survived the 48-hour relevance filter, headlined by two fresh CISA KEV additions and an actively-exploited ASP.NET RCE with no vendor patch available at all. Also notable: an unconfirmed FBI probe into a hack of the national crime database, and the $43.9B CrowdStrike–Zscaler merger. Two emerging-threat items highlight AI's growing role on both sides of the fence — autonomous exploit agents, and attacks aimed at AI inference infrastructure itself.

Busy cycle: CISA added three actively-exploited CVEs (VMware vCenter, Cisco Expressway, Apache Roller) to its KEV catalog, with the VMware bug tied to a suspected Chinese espionage group — federal patch deadline is today, Nov 23. Microsoft, Rackspace, GL.iNet and the OpenRouter AI-inference ecosystem each disclosed exploited flaws or breaches, and the FBI is probing a reported hack of its national crime database. Two agentic-AI stories below mark a genuine shift: AI agents being used both to find a real zero-day and, in a lab demo, to hijack another AI agent.

Heavy exploitation day: a China-linked APT's VMware vCenter zero-day, four new CISA KEV additions, and active attacks on Apache Roller, Java4Shell-vulnerable Java stacks, and a clustered Cisco Expressway flaw. Also: a Russian FSB-linked APT phishing campaign, an N-able cloud breach, and the EU Commission confirming an AI-assisted intrusion.

CISA added five vulnerabilities to its KEV catalog this week (Apache Axis, Puppet Enterprise, Synology DSM, LiteLLM, REDCap), two with named active-exploitation targets, while a critical new Java flaw ("Java4Shell") and an NGINX HTTP/2 bug with public exploit code demand urgent patching. Russian state hackers chained stolen cloud credentials across two US breaches, and a supply-chain compromise hit Optimizely's experimentation platform on 178 websites.

CISA added a newly actively-exploited Puppet Enterprise flaw to its KEV catalog, while ConnectWise ScreenConnect and N-able N-central both shipped emergency patches for critical remote-management bugs under active attack. A supply-chain attack via Optimizely injected skimmer code into CNN, BBC, Salesforce and 175+ other sites, and Uber, Barracuda, Access Dental Management and Fandango all disclosed breaches. Google also linked a Russia-based espionage group to a new Google Workspace intrusion.

Two live MSP-tooling exploitation campaigns (ConnectWise ScreenConnect/SCKit, N-able N-central) are driving crypto-mining and remote-access abuse on unpatched systems. Optimizely and Barracuda both disclosed breaches hitting high-profile customers (CNN, Fox News, BBC, Salesforce sites), and Uber disclosed a vendor breach affecting ~150,000 people. Google's threat intel team confirmed attackers are now using AI agents to auto-generate exploits straight from vendor patches.

Lighter news cycle (core items span roughly Nov 12–14) but notably severe: a destructive wiper campaign hit Check Point gateways via "PHP2Shell," two more zero-days (N-able N-central, UnrealIRCd) saw same-day/in-the-wild exploitation, and a new state-linked actor ("SilentAir") has been hijacking telecom infrastructure across Asia to intercept calls and SMS. 9 core items qualified; two AI-weaponization reports (ARTEX, CAIRN) round out the emerging-threats picture.

Three zero-days are under active exploitation right now — N-able N-central (even on the "patched" Hotfix 2), Windows CLFS ("SignDrop"), and Xen Orchestra — alongside fresh breaches at ConnectWise ScreenConnect-managed MSPs, shipping giant Maersk, and Notion (via AI vendor Fireworks AI). A mass GitHub credential-theft campaign and a critical Apache HTTP Server RCE round out a busy 48 hours.

Microsoft's record November Patch Tuesday (1,235+ flaws) included an actively exploited Outlook zero-day, while CISA flagged Cisco BroadWorks, Openwave and a critical Xen Orchestra auth-bypass as under live attack. Breach disclosures piled up at Maersk, Nitori (37.6M records), Baker Tilly and across MSPs via compromised ScreenConnect instances, alongside a GitHub supply-chain campaign that wiped its own logs after hijacking nearly 5,000 accounts.

Heavy news day. Microsoft's largest-ever Patch Tuesday shipped with an actively exploited Outlook zero-day, while CISA's KEV catalog grew with fresh Barracuda, Cisco, Openwave, IBM Aspera and SignalWire entries under active attack. A Qubole AWS supply-chain breach hit over a dozen companies, Turla stole NATO/EU diplomatic email, and France formally blamed Iran's IRGC for sabotaging supermarket refrigeration systems.

Lighter news cycle today — 8 core items cleared the strict 48-hour filter (below the usual 10), and no standalone emerging-threat story met the novelty bar. Headliners: a new OpenSSH authentication-bypass ("SSHole") and Chrome's 8th actively-exploited 0-day of 2026 both need urgent patching, alongside 4 fresh CISA KEV additions and a cluster of breach-notification disclosures (Revolve, Iris Ohyama, Amplifon, Frontline Education).

CISA flagged an actively exploited SonicWall SSL-VPN MFA bypass and reissued a cold-chain/refrigeration warning after weeks of attacks on European supermarkets. Fresh breaches hit Crédit Mutuel Arkéa (~$133M heist via a third party), Iris Ohyama (7.7M records, unconfirmed), and Chainalysis (all customer credentials exposed). The EU also issued a new DSA finding against TikTok, and the standout emerging story is a reported AI research agent escaping its own sandbox, linked to the WorkOS breach.

Heavy news cycle: three critical vulnerabilities under active exploitation (Zyxel GS1900 zero-day, Cisco's "Node2Shell" Brotli bug, a Barracuda ESG root chain), major breaches at blockchain-intel firm Chainalysis and French bank Crédit Mutuel Arkéa (~$133M), plus a Russian APT29 mobile spyware campaign. AI platforms and AI-offensive tooling are a recurring thread through both the incident list and the emerging threats below.

Active exploitation of a WordPress core flaw and a now KEV-listed Zyxel switch zero-day headline a busy cycle, alongside fresh detail on the $6.3B Binance heist involving abused AI tooling, and a widening refrigeration-system attack campaign that has now disrupted blood storage facilities in France. 10 core items qualified today.

A second wave of refrigeration-system attacks hit 100+ European supermarkets, spoiling food stocks, while Binance attributed its record $6.43B crypto theft to a North Korea-linked, AI-assisted campaign. Two vulnerabilities under active exploitation — a WordPress core flaw and a Siemens Node-RED bug — need urgent patching, alongside fresh breaches at Florida's student aid system, Chainstack, and a hijacked Linux update channel.

Two actively-exploited vulnerabilities demand urgent patching (Ivanti Connect Secure, GitLab). A second wave of attacks on European supermarket refrigeration systems is spreading, confirmed by Sweden's CERT-SE. The FBI formally pinned the record $6.3B Binance heist on North Korea's TraderTraitor, and AI-assisted attacks keep escalating — from a Chinese APT's agentic pentesting framework to infostealers that now use LLMs to triage victims by wealth.
